heading: Weather and Atmospheric Science
description: Fifty illustrated topics exploring winds, towering storm clouds, lightning, hailstones, rainfall, and our protective upper sky.

entries.title: Clouds being driven by winds
entries.scientific_finding: Clouds are transported by atmospheric winds, with their movement depending on wind speed and direction at different altitudes.
entries.connection: The verses describe winds driving clouds before rainfall.
entries.limitations: They do not provide a technical account of atmospheric circulation or cloud dynamics.

research_rules: Verify every Quran reference, Arabic word and translation before publication.
Read the complete passage and its surrounding verses.
Consult classical tafsir before assigning a modern meteorological meaning.
Distinguish Quranic wording from classical interpretation and modern scientific explanation.
Do not claim that every cloud produces rain.
Do not claim that the Quran explicitly explains modern cloud microphysics.
Do not claim that the word fertilizing in 15:22 has only one scientific interpretation.
Do not equate mountain-like cloud imagery with a modern cloud classification without linguistic and tafsir evidence.
Do not claim that every rainstorm has the same formation mechanism.
Do not invent hadith, authenticity grades, scientific papers, authors or publication details.
Use authoritative meteorological institutions and peer-reviewed research for specific scientific claims.
Treat evidence grades as provisional and revise them after detailed research.
A similarity between a verse and a scientific observation is not automatically a scientific miracle.

research_scope.purpose: Source-linked research draft for evaluating the 50 original weather and atmospheric topic candidates; not a declaration that all are scientific miracles.

research_scope.grading_note: Original evidence grades are preserved unchanged and remain provisional; links to general meteorology sources do not justify upgrading a grade.

NOAA_CLOUDS.title: Clouds
NOAA_CLOUDS.supports: Clouds are visible aggregates of tiny liquid water droplets and/or ice crystals; clouds can be transported by winds and affect sunlight and temperature.

NOAA_CLOUD_FORMATION.title: How Clouds Form
NOAA_CLOUD_FORMATION.supports: Cloud condensation nuclei, saturation, cooling of rising air, condensation, and ongoing evaporation/condensation within clouds.

NOAA_CLOUD_TYPES.title: Ten Basic Clouds
NOAA_CLOUD_TYPES.supports: Cloud forms including cumulonimbus; thunderstorm clouds can have great vertical extent and produce precipitation, hail and tornadoes.

NOAA_PRECIPITATION.title: Precipitation
NOAA_PRECIPITATION.supports: Moisture transport, lifting, cloud formation, collision-coalescence and ice-crystal precipitation processes.

NOAA_THUNDERSTORM_LIFE.title: Life Cycle of a Thunderstorm
NOAA_THUNDERSTORM_LIFE.supports: Thunderstorm updrafts, downdrafts, mature-stage hazards, heavy precipitation, hail and damaging winds.

NOAA_LIGHTNING.title: How Lightning is Created
NOAA_LIGHTNING.supports: Charge separation in thunderstorms through collisions among ice particles, graupel and supercooled droplets.

NWS_LIGHTNING_SAFETY.title: Lightning: What You Need to Know
NWS_LIGHTNING_SAFETY.supports: Lightning hazards and practical safety guidance; thunder indicates nearby lightning risk.

NASA_OZONE_UV.supports: Stratospheric ozone absorbs much biologically harmful UV radiation; atmospheric protection is specific, not a complete shield against all hazards.

NASA_ATMOSPHERE.supports: Atmosphere supplies breathable air, helps regulate temperature and protects life from harmful ultraviolet radiation.

critical_cautions: Clouds consist of liquid droplets and/or ice crystals; not every cloud produces precipitation.
Cloud formation depends on moisture, nuclei, cooling and saturation; avoid reducing all cloud formation to one mechanism.
The phrase 'winds that fertilize' in 15:22 has interpretive range and should not be asserted to mean only wind pollination.
The mountain-like cloud imagery in 24:43 should not automatically be identified with a specific modern cloud type or used as proof of detailed cloud microphysics.
Lightning is an electrical discharge associated with charge separation in storms; thunder is the sound associated with rapid heating and expansion of air, not the same phenomenon as lightning.
Hail forms in suitable storm updraft and supercooled-water conditions; not every storm cloud produces hail.
The atmosphere provides several forms of protection, including UV absorption by stratospheric ozone and thermal regulation, but it is not an absolute shield.
Clouds can both reflect incoming sunlight and absorb/trap outgoing infrared radiation; their net effect depends on cloud properties and context.
Rain can remove some aerosols and soluble substances from air, but 'rain as purification' should not be turned into a claim that rain sterilizes or makes all water safe.
Historical destructive-wind passages should not be treated as a forecast model or as proof that every severe wind event has the same meteorological cause.
